about:
> *Half Life is the unfortunate condition of all things.*
>
> Nothing maintains its proper shape for very long. Cities rearrange themselves. Familiar places disappear. Friends scatter toward distant shores. Great enthusiasms become mild curiosities, and occasionally the reverse. Even you, despite whatever assurances you may have made on the subject, are becoming someone else.
>
> This is generally considered alarming.
>
> I have elected to find it interesting.
>
> Half Life is my attempt to keep some record of the transformation: photographs, journeys, projects, people, objects, observations, and whatever peculiar business happens to occupy my attention before it inevitably gives way to something else.
>
> I make no promise that these records will be complete, useful, or even entirely sensible. Completeness is an exhausting ambition, and usefulness has already been addressed elsewhere on this site.
>
> The important thing is that one remains conscious. Still looking. Still wanting. Still wandering about with unreasonable plans.
>
> Everything is already changing.
>
> One may as well go see what it becomes.
bestiary_intro:
In these latter days, when the old red sun gutters like a lamp short of oil and may at any hour go dark, a prudent man keeps account of what he has taken from the world before the world is done with him.

Herein are set down the denizens of the cold lakes of California, each drawn forth by rod, line and low cunning. The weights are exact. As to the rest, the angler entertains no disputes and offers no refunds.

posts.title: Entry 000002
posts.body:
With so many matters presently in motion, I have decided that further contemplation of the past would constitute an irresponsible misuse of the present. The old accounts may wait. There are expeditions to organize.

In the days soon to come, I intend to assemble a small but exceptionally capable company of men and sail for Treasure Island. Our purpose is singular and, I believe, culturally significant: to capture the finest photograph yet made of the San Francisco skyline. Should we succeed, the resulting image shall be displayed here at some considerably later date, once sufficient time has passed for the public to receive it properly.

For this undertaking I shall require two or three men of various builds, temperaments, and useful dispositions.

First, a land surveyor: one intimately familiar with the city, its peculiar geography, its winds, elevations, secret prospects, and the many locations from which San Francisco most enjoys being admired.

Second, a pack hauler: of sturdy constitution and cheerful obedience, who shall relieve me of those instruments necessary to my art but whose weight I find personally objectionable.

Finally, a charming fellow: of easy speech and flexible principle, whose purpose shall be to secure our passage through ports, gates, checkpoints, and whatever minor authorities presume to stand between us and destiny.

I shall, naturally, assume the role of mystic: consulting the heavens, interpreting the light, inspecting cloud formations with grave concern, and periodically pointing toward the horizon as though privy to information unavailable to ordinary men.

If all perform their duties admirably, glory is probable.

My second voyage shall be grander still.

By airship I shall depart for a distant island, a place reputed to restore both body and soul and return a weary traveler to civilization with an improved complexion and considerably better opinions about life.

I have visited this island before and can personally attest that the legends are true. Indeed, my spirit remains somewhat irresponsibly ignited from my previous pilgrimage. I therefore return in pursuit of those mysteries that escaped me the first time: warm waters, magnificent meals, long and idle afternoons, and that gentle breeze drifting in from parts unknown, carrying upon it the sweet scent of youth.

For an expedition of this importance, one cannot travel with ordinary company.

I shall therefore be accompanied by a woman of singular distinction, my girlfriend.

Her qualifications are numerous and difficult to summarize without embarrassing lesser persons. She possesses excellent taste, formidable curiosity, an instinctive understanding of beauty, and the rare ability to enter a place and immediately improve its general condition. Where I tend toward maps, equipment, unnecessary schemes, and solemn declarations of purpose, she possesses the considerably rarer faculty of knowing what is actually worth doing.

She is neither porter, assistant, nor decorative passenger. She travels under her own authority.

She too seeks the legends.

Indeed, I suspect the island may surrender certain secrets to her which it has deliberately concealed from me. This possibility is irritating, but I have made peace with it.

Fortunately, we shall not wander blindly.

Awaiting us is a guide most trusted, a man whom I consider a close brother and whom my companion already knows well.

It is difficult to describe this man without appearing to exaggerate, and so I shall make no attempt to restrain myself.

He is possessed of such uncommon ability that, were ambition his principal defect, entire institutions might presently operate according to his whims. He could, I suspect, bend the wills of sensible men toward almost any design and have them thanking him afterward for the privilege.

Yet he has chosen peace.

He lives humbly. He crests one mountain only to discover another behind it. He counts the grains of sand and, rather than declaring himself master of the coast, concludes that he has yet to understand the beach.

Such men are inconveniently rare.

His studies are now drawing to a close, and soon he will seek some grander stage upon which to deploy his talents. What form that stage shall take, I cannot say. I only know that the world will shortly have to contend with him.

Before that hour arrives, however, I intend to meet him upon this island one final time.

Thus the voyage carries purposes beyond leisure. I go to restore the spirit, pursue certain legendary gifts, rediscover an enchanted place beside a woman of extraordinary consequence, and share a few more idle days with a brother before the currents of life carry us toward different shores.

There will also, I am told, be drinks with little umbrellas in them.

The island awaits.

posts.title: Entry 000001
posts.body:
Hello,

For some considerable time I have entertained the notion that I ought to have a website. The reasons for this conviction remain somewhat obscure, but the conviction itself has proved remarkably durable. At last, through a combination of industry, vanity, and an unexpected abundance of free time, the thing now exists.

My present scheme is to begin with several long and shamelessly retrospective accounts of the year thus far: projects undertaken with varying degrees of competence, places visited, objects made, and other episodes which, through the generous distortions of memory, now seem worthy of documentation.

Whether any of this will prove useful to anyone is doubtful. Fortunately, usefulness was never among the requirements.

Once I have exhausted accounts of the recent past, I shall concern myself with the future.

bestiary.name: Rainbow Trout
bestiary.lore:
Of the demons that haunt Pine Lake, this is held to be the most irascible. The savant Ombalique, who spent eleven years cataloguing its moods from the safety of the shore, pronounced it "a creature of fastidious malice, striped in the colors of a sunset it did not deserve."

It keeps to the cold deeps where the light fails, and rises at dusk to take whatever is foolish enough to touch the surface. Those who have hooked it report a pull of unreasonable vigor, and afterward a persistent sense of having been appraised and found wanting.

When it leaps, the ignorant suppose it wishes to escape. The wise know it merely wishes to see who has presumed.

bestiary.name: Sunfish
bestiary.lore:
A small round personage of the shallows, gilded like a coin and very nearly as common. It guards its patch of gravel with a ferocity out of all proportion to its size, and will rush at intruders many times larger: a policy that philosophers have called valiant and fishermen have called convenient.

Along the lakeshore it is agreed that to catch one confers no distinction, and that to catch none is a disgrace.

bestiary.name: Crappie
bestiary.lore:
A pale, speckled fish of retiring habit, which gathers among sunken thickets with others of its kind and conducts its affairs chiefly at dawn and dusk. Its mouth is thin as wet parchment and tears at the least insistence, whence the vulgar name of papermouth.

The angler who hauls too eagerly is left holding a bare hook and an improved understanding of patience.

bestiary.name: Bass
bestiary.lore:
A stout green brigand that lurks beside drowned timber and awaits events. Its mouth is of extraordinary capacity, and it regards whatever passes as a meal first and a question of suitability afterward.

It is the fish that every lake angler professes to find commonplace and privately desires above all others. To land one is to be insufferable for a week.

bestiary.name: Catfish
bestiary.lore:
A whiskered dignitary of the lake bottom, smooth as a river stone and wholly without scales, which it appears to regard as an affectation of lesser fish. It goes abroad by night, tasting the mud with its barbels and finding nothing beneath its notice.

The spines of its fins deliver a sharp rebuke to careless hands. Those so instructed seldom require a second lesson.

bestiary.name: Striped Bass
bestiary.lore: Fishermen of the Bay speak of a silver brute, barred along the flank like a convict, that runs the channels on a moving tide and breaks whatever tackle is offered it. Each claims to have hooked one. None can produce it.

bestiary.name: California Halibut
bestiary.lore: Said to lie flat upon the sand with both eyes on one side of its head, an arrangement it finds convenient and others find unsettling. It does not pursue. It waits, and what passes overhead ceases to pass.

bestiary.name: Brown Trout
bestiary.lore: A sullen recluse of the undercut bank, spotted in red and black, which feeds at dusk and trusts nothing that arrives by daylight.

bestiary.name: Brook Trout
bestiary.lore: A small bright thing of the cold headwaters, speckled like a jeweller's sample tray, and so greedy that it is held to be no test of skill whatever.

bestiary.name: Golden Trout
bestiary.location: The High Sierra, above ten thousand feet
bestiary.lore: It is said to live only where the air is too thin for reasonable men, and to wear the colors of a sunset that the lower world is no longer permitted to see.

bestiary.name: Lahontan Cutthroat Trout
bestiary.lore: An old lineage of the desert lakes, marked beneath the jaw with a slash of red, as though it had survived an attempt upon its life and wished the fact known.

bestiary.name: Lake Trout
bestiary.lore: It keeps to depths where no light arrives and no line is long enough, and grows there to a size that those who have seen it decline to state.

bestiary.name: Kokanee Salmon
bestiary.lore: A silver wanderer that never saw the sea its ancestors knew, and in autumn turns scarlet with what may be regret.

bestiary.name: Chinook Salmon
bestiary.location: The Sacramento River and the open coast
bestiary.lore: The king of its kind returns from the ocean to the river of its birth, fat with years of plunder, to die in the gravel where it began. It does not go quietly.

bestiary.name: Steelhead
bestiary.lore: The fish of a thousand casts. It enters the rivers on the winter rains, grey as the weather, and is gone again before the water clears.

bestiary.name: Smallmouth Bass
bestiary.lore: A bronze brawler of rocky water, smaller than its cousin and of twice the temper.

bestiary.name: Spotted Bass
bestiary.lore: It suspends itself in deep clear water over nothing at all, and regards a lure for a long time before declining it.

bestiary.name: Bluegill
bestiary.lore: The first fish of every angler and the last resort of many. It bites at anything, including bare hooks and, on occasion, toes.

bestiary.name: Redear Sunfish
bestiary.lore: A grubber of the lake floor that cracks snails between its teeth with a sound, it is claimed, audible from the bank.

bestiary.name: Brown Bullhead
bestiary.lore: A small whiskered person of the mud, who thrives in water that would kill anything of refinement and seems proud of it.

bestiary.name: Common Carp
bestiary.lore: A great bronze vacuum of the shallows, despised by the fastidious and pursued in secret by those who have felt one run.

bestiary.name: Sacramento Pikeminnow
bestiary.lore: A long grey native with the appetite of a bandit, which was here before the dams and expects to remain after them.

bestiary.name: American Shad
bestiary.location: The Sacramento and American Rivers in spring
bestiary.lore: It comes up from the sea in silver thousands when the cottonwoods shed, and fights like a fish of three times its weight.

bestiary.name: White Sturgeon
bestiary.location: The Delta and San Pablo Bay
bestiary.lore: Armored in bony plates and older than most nations, it roots along the bottom of the bay as it did when the bay was new. Some are longer than the boats that seek them.

bestiary.name: Signal Crayfish
bestiary.lore: A small armored brigand that walks backward from every argument with its claws raised, conceding nothing.

bestiary.name: Pacific Sanddab
bestiary.lore: A modest flat creature the size of a hand, which lies on the sand in multitudes and is prized chiefly by cooks.

bestiary.name: Starry Flounder
bestiary.lore: Its fins are banded orange and black like a herald's banner, the only vanity it permits itself.

bestiary.name: Black Rockfish
bestiary.location: Kelp and reefs of the north coast
bestiary.lore: A dark schooling fish of the kelp, which rises to the surface at evening in such numbers that the water appears to boil.

bestiary.name: Vermilion Rockfish
bestiary.lore: Red as a cardinal's robe and bristling with spines, it lives long past a century in water where color has no witness.

bestiary.name: Cabezon
bestiary.lore: A mottled glutton that is mostly head. It swallows crabs entire and lies so still among the rocks that anglers have stood upon it.

bestiary.name: Lingcod
bestiary.lore: A long ill-tempered ambusher with a mouth full of needles, known to seize a hooked fish and refuse to let go even at the gaff.

bestiary.name: Barred Surfperch
bestiary.lore: A silver fish with rust-colored bars that feeds in the wash of breaking waves, in water barely deep enough to cover it.

bestiary.name: Redtail Surfperch
bestiary.lore: It works the steep cold beaches of the north, and shows a flash of rose at the tail as it turns in the foam.

bestiary.name: Jacksmelt
bestiary.lore: A slender silver nuisance of every pier, taken six at a time by children and regarded by serious men as bait.

bestiary.name: Pacific Mackerel
bestiary.lore: A green-backed rover that travels in ravenous companies and will strike a bare gold hook out of plain enthusiasm.

bestiary.name: Pacific Bonito
bestiary.lore: A striped projectile of the warm currents that hits like a thrown brick and bleeds like a stuck pig.

bestiary.name: Yellowtail
bestiary.lore: A gold-striped bruiser that, once hooked, runs directly for the nearest rock and saws the line across it with evident purpose.

bestiary.name: Bluefin Tuna
bestiary.lore: A warm-blooded engine the weight of several men, which crosses oceans as others cross a street. Those who have fought one speak of it afterward in lowered voices.

bestiary.name: Kelp Bass
bestiary.lore: A checkered loiterer among the kelp stalks, which takes the bait and retires into the weed before the angler has finished congratulating himself.

bestiary.name: California Sheephead
bestiary.lore: The male is black at both ends and red in the middle, with the teeth of a dog. Each began life as a female, a matter on which it offers no comment.

bestiary.name: White Seabass
bestiary.lore: The grey ghost. It moves along the kelp edge in darkness making a sound like a croaking door, and is seldom seen by those who seek it hardest.

bestiary.name: Leopard Shark
bestiary.lore: A slender spotted shark that cruises the mudflats on the rising tide, harmless to all but clams and worms.

bestiary.name: Sevengill Shark
bestiary.location: The deep channels of the Bay
bestiary.lore: An ancient pattern of shark, with more gills than are now customary, that patrols the cold channels beneath the bridge and eats whatever it finds there, including other sharks.

bestiary.name: Bat Ray
bestiary.lore: A dark kite of the mudflats that beats its wings against the bottom to uncover its dinner, and when hooked departs for the open sea without discussion.

bestiary.name: Dungeness Crab
bestiary.location: Cold sand off the north coast
bestiary.lore: A broad purple-backed crab of excellent flavor and poor disposition, taken in winter by those willing to be cold and wet.

bestiary.name: Red Rock Crab
bestiary.lore: A brick-red scavenger with black-tipped claws of surprising authority. It yields little meat and a great deal of opinion.

bestiary.name: California Spiny Lobster
bestiary.lore: It has no claws and wants none, relying upon spines, long whips of antennae, and a habit of backing into holes exactly its own size.

bestiary.name: Market Squid
bestiary.lore: They rise to lamplight in pale flickering thousands, changing color as they come, and are gone by morning as if the sea had dreamed them.

places.name: Chengdu
places.note: A city of teahouses, peppercorns and deliberate idleness, where the citizens have raised the afternoon nap to a civic art. The cuisine is designed to numb the mouth so that the visitor cannot complain of the heat, and the district's most celebrated residents are black and white, eat only bamboo, and decline all interviews.

places.name: China and Hong Kong
places.note:
An empire so old that its ruins have ruins, and so large that a man may travel for three weeks by the fastest trains yet devised and see only a corner of it. Its cities are built by the hundred million and lit like festivals; its mountains were plainly designed by a painter; its cooks regard no part of any animal as beyond discussion.

Marked here are the places reached in the spring of 2026, and beside them the great sights still owing: a wall, a buried army, a palace on the roof of the world. The list is not short. The empire is patient.

places.name: Chongqing
places.note: A city built on the theory that the ground is optional. Its towers climb out of the fog at every angle, its trains pass through the apartments of the citizens without apology, and what the map calls the first floor may be the twentieth upon inquiry.

places.name: Guangzhou
places.note: An old trading port where anything may be had for a price and the price is never the first one mentioned. Jade is weighed here by the hundredweight, breakfast is served in forty small baskets, and perfume is studied with the gravity other cities reserve for law.

places.name: Hattiesburg
places.note: A pine-country town at the meeting of two railways, called the Hub City by those who feel the title requires no further defense. The traveler finds here a long green trail where the trains once ran, and a museum kept in an alley.

places.name: Hong Kong
places.note: A city stacked upon a rock, where the towers crowd to the water's edge like spectators at an execution. A green ferry has crossed the harbor every few minutes for longer than anyone can recall, and at night the whole place is lit as if to signal something very far away.

places.name: Lake Chabot
places.note: A reservoir in the eastern hills, dug in a former age to water a city and since given over to anglers, who line its banks at dawn in attitudes of patient suspicion. The catfish arrive by truck, a fact the catfish do not discuss.

places.name: Meridian
places.note: Once the largest city of its state and still inclined to mention it. An antique carousel turns in the park as it has for a century, the father of country music is remembered in a small museum, and one tall ornamented tower surveys the rest with composure.

places.name: New Orleans
places.note: A city below the level of its own river, which it regards as a technicality. The dead are kept above ground, the music is kept in the street, and the hour at which one ought to go home has never been established to anyone's satisfaction.

places.name: Ojai
places.note: A small valley town among orange groves, much favored by mystics, potters and persons recovering from Los Angeles. At sunset the mountains to the east turn the color of a ripe peach, and the population stops in the street to approve.

places.name: Pine Lake
places.note: A cold clear lake in the pine country, ringed by granite and held in place by a dam of respectable age. The hills hereabouts are hollow: caverns run beneath them hung with stone icicles, into which travelers are lowered on ropes for their own amusement.

places.name: San Francisco
places.note:
Home. A city of forty-odd hills at the end of a peninsula, wrapped most mornings in a fog so thick that the residents have given it a name and speak of it as a neighbor. The streets were laid out by a man with a ruler and no regard for the terrain, so that they proceed directly up slopes a goat would decline.

The Mission, in the sunny lee of the hills, is where this log is kept. It is older than the city around it, loud at all hours, painted on every available wall, and warmer than the rest by a margin its inhabitants will mention unprompted.

places.name: Shanghai
places.note: On one bank of the river stand the counting-houses of a vanished empire; on the other, towers raised by its successors to look down upon them. The traveler is invited to stand between and draw his own conclusions, preferably after shopping.

places.name: Washington, DC
places.note: The capital, laid out in avenues wide enough to march an army down, as has occasionally been necessary. Its citizens have assembled the treasures of the continent in marble halls and charge nothing to view them, a liberality unknown in lesser empires.

places.name: Zhangjiajie
places.note: Three thousand pillars of stone stand here in a sea of mist, as though some sorcerer had begun a forest and lost interest before the leaves. The inhabitants have since attached elevators to the cliffs and paved the abysses with glass, on the theory that vertigo may be charged for.

quests.title: The Mending of the Bottomless Bag
quests.body: The bag has no bottom, a property much admired until the zipper failed. It now stands open at all hours, and things once put safely away have begun to wander back out. No tailor of the district will take the work: the last to try has not been seen since he reached in for the pull.

roles.name: Owner of the Bag
roles.about: Bears the cost, and the blame for having let it come to this

roles.name: Mender
roles.about: A tailor of steady hand, willing to look inside

roles.name: Holder of the Lamp
roles.about: Holds the light over the work and does not look down

roles.name: Witness
roles.about: Keeps the account of whatever has already fallen out

objectives.text: Find a mender willing to look inside
Procure a zipper of sufficient length
Account for whatever has already fallen out
Close the bag
Refrain from asking what is at the bottom

quests.title: The Cold Lakes
quests.body: A company goes up into the high country in the last days of the season, when the aspens have spent their gold and the lakes are making up their minds to freeze. The trout there are fat, slow, and of the opinion that the year is over. They are to be corrected.
quests.reward: Fat trout, numb hands, and the right to speak of it

roles.name: Master of the Rod
roles.about: Decides where the fish are, and is answerable when they are elsewhere

roles.name: Coachman
roles.about: Drives the company up into the high country and, it is hoped, back down

roles.name: Boatman
roles.about: Rows the hired boat and keeps his opinions of the fishing to himself

roles.name: Camp Cook
roles.about: Feeds the company before dawn and makes something of whatever is caught

roles.name: Keeper of the Fire
roles.about: Lights it, feeds it, and is blamed when it goes out

roles.name: Net Man
roles.about: Stands ready at the bank and does not miss

objectives.text: Take the sullen recluse of the undercut bank
Take a speckled glutton of the headwaters
Fish the high lake from a hired boat
Walk once around the lake of the fugitives
Endure one dawn below freezing without complaint

quests.title: The Islands of Fire
quests.body: Far out upon the western ocean lies a chain of islands that the sea did not want and the earth insisted upon. One is still under construction: the ground there glows by night, and the inhabitants make offerings to the mountain and build their houses elsewhere.
quests.reward: A darker complexion, and sand in everything owned

roles.name: Pilgrim
roles.about: Goes to be restored in body and soul, and to return with better opinions

roles.name: Woman of Singular Distinction
roles.about: Travels under her own authority; knows what is actually worth doing

roles.name: Guide Most Trusted
roles.about: A brother of the island, who counts the sand and claims no mastery of the beach

roles.name: Warden of the Green
roles.about: Stays behind and waters the plants; the last holder of this post is not spoken of

roles.name: Keeper of the Post
roles.about: Minds the door and gathers what the couriers leave in the keeper's absence

objectives.text: Stand at the rim of the burning mountain
Climb the dead crater above the city
Pass a night in the village beneath the fire
Make a likeness of ground not yet a year old
Visit the hall where the island kings kept their feathers

quests.title: The Voyage to Treasure Island
quests.when: In the days soon to come
quests.body:
A small but exceptionally capable company is to be assembled and sail for Treasure Island. The purpose is singular and culturally significant: to capture the finest photograph yet made of the San Francisco skyline.

Two or three men are required, of various builds, temperaments and useful dispositions: a land surveyor, a pack hauler, and a charming fellow to secure passage through ports, gates, checkpoints, and whatever minor authorities presume to stand between the company and destiny. The post of mystic is filled. The keeper will consult the heavens, interpret the light, and point toward the horizon as required.

Those who would join should choose a post below and petition for it. If all perform their duties admirably, glory is probable.
quests.reward: The finest photograph yet made of the San Francisco skyline

roles.name: Mystic
roles.about: Consults the heavens, interprets the light, points toward the horizon

roles.name: Land Surveyor
roles.about: Knows the city, its winds, elevations and secret prospects

roles.name: Pack Hauler
roles.about: Of sturdy constitution and cheerful obedience; carries the instruments

roles.name: Charming Fellow
roles.about: Of easy speech and flexible principle; secures passage past minor authorities

objectives.text: Engage a land surveyor, familiar with the city, its winds and its secret prospects
Engage a pack hauler of sturdy constitution and cheerful obedience
Engage a charming fellow of easy speech and flexible principle
Sail for Treasure Island
Capture the finest photograph yet made of the San Francisco skyline

plants.name: Queen Anthurium
plants.light: Bright shade; never the sun itself
plants.lore: A velvet aristocrat from the cloud forests, with leaves as long as a man's arm and the complexion of a banker's waistcoat. She requires air so wet that it may be wrung out, and regards any departure from this as a personal affront, which she expresses by browning at the edges.

plants.name: Philodendron Gloriosum
plants.water: When the top of the soil has dried
plants.lore: A creeping thing that will not climb, though every other member of its family does, and offers no reason. Its leaves are hearts of green velvet ruled with white, each unfurling over a period of weeks, during which it must not be looked at too directly. Two are kept, in case one should take offense.

plants.name: Monstera Thai Constellation
plants.lore: A plant splashed with cream as though someone had flicked a paintbrush at the night sky. It was devised in a laboratory in the East and for some years could be had only by the rich or the reckless. The holes in its leaves are deliberate, and it grows more of them as it gains confidence.

plants.name: Howard's Dream
plants.lore: An orchid of no natural ancestry: four separate kinds were persuaded into one by growers who could not leave well enough alone. It sends up a spike of dark stars, spotted and edged in white, and holds them for two months. Who Howard was is not recorded, nor whether the dream was a pleasant one.

plants.name: Juniper
plants.lore: Two low green junipers, the customary first trees of every beginner and the customary first losses. They are hardy to the point of insolence and will endure frost, wind and neglect of nearly every kind. The exception is a missed watering in warm weather, of which they do not complain: they simply remain green for several weeks after they have died, out of spite.

plants.name: Maple Grove
plants.lore: A stand of small maples planted together in one tray to resemble a wood seen from a great distance. In autumn they turned the red of a magistrate's robe, and visitors were made to admire them. Maples drink without pause and forgive nothing. The leaves crisped first, then the twigs, and the wood was a wood no longer.

plants.name: Grape Vine
plants.lore: A grape vine persuaded, against its whole nature, to remain the height of a man's forearm. It bore each year a single cluster of grapes of the ordinary size, which hung from it like a chandelier from a footstool. It was the most admired tree in the collection, and so naturally the first to go.

plants.name: Redwood Grove
plants.lore: A grove of coast redwoods, a tree that left to itself lives two thousand years and stands taller than a cathedral. These were kept a foot high in a dish. They are creatures of the fog and take their water from the air as much as the soil; deprived of both they went the color of rust in a fortnight. Their wild cousins a few miles north did not notice.

plants_intro.bonsai:
---

Let it be recorded that every tree in this collection perished while its keeper was away in the far East.

They had been shaped with wire and patience over a period of a year, and asked of the world only water: daily, and without fail. Arrangements were made. The arrangements did not hold. They are set down here as they were, that their names not be lost along with them. To be revieved in the weeks to come.
plants_intro.house: The plants of the house, which ask for little: filtered light, damp air, and to be left out of their keeper's travel plans. Unlike the trees, these yet live.

status.name: Chris
status.body: A keeper of records, by his own appointment. He carries a camera into places where it is unwelcome, a rod to waters where the fish have other plans, and a notebook in which he sets down both encounters to his own advantage.
